Research Questions — Key Findings 3 Experiments
Question 1
Is it possible to predict % Silica Concentrate every minute?
Yes. By resampling sensor data to 1-minute intervals and engineering lag features (past 1, 5, 10, 30, 60 minutes) plus rolling statistics, XGBoost achieves RMSE = 0.7534 and R² = 0.5692 on the held-out test set. The model captures the short-term dynamics of the flotation process effectively. Minute-level lag features of the target (autoregressive features) are the most important predictors.
✅ Yes — Feasible (R² = 0.5692)
Question 2
How many steps (hours) ahead can we predict % Silica Concentrate?
Separate XGBoost models were trained for 1h, 2h, 4h, 8h, and 12h forecast horizons. Performance degrades as the horizon increases — which is expected for industrial time series. 1h ahead shows best accuracy. At 12 hours ahead, RMSE rises to 1.1465 (R² = 0.0017). This gives plant engineers a practical early-warning window to take corrective actions.
⏱ 1h ahead shows best accuracy
Question 3
Is it possible to predict % Silica without using % Iron Concentrate (highly correlated)?
The correlation between % Iron Concentrate and % Silica Concentrate is r = -0.8012 — highly negative. When the % Iron Concentrate column is removed and the model is retrained, RMSE changes from 0.7534 → 0.7548 (Δ = +0.0014), and R² changes from 0.5692 → 0.5677 (Δ = -0.0015). The model without iron still leverages process variables (airflow, flotation column levels) to make useful predictions.
⚠ Degraded — Iron feature significantly helps
